title: Cross-asset dual momentum
body:
Raising assets for a transparent monthly ETF portfolio
Research-stage B3: risk cap, explicit cash, no leverage
CAGR 6.89% | daily max drawdown -17.91%
Illustrative USD 10 million mandate; execution validation starts with a USD 1 million scenario
notes: ETF capital: 2007-08-31 execution inception to 2026-08-31; modeled net 10 bps/traded dollar. Objective is raising assets, not working capital. Performance is historical and mixed; no live readiness. Hanyu Zhang, FINCB9339 Homework 2.

title: Momentum strategy landscape
body:
Buy-and-hold: continuous market exposure
Relative momentum: rank assets against peers
Absolute momentum: compare an asset with its cash hurdle
Our dual design: three selected ETF slots, failed slots to cash
Futures CTAs can short declining markets; this portfolio cannot
notes: Lecture slides 4-7, 22-23, 42-44; Asness et al. 2014 pp 2-4. Stock momentum ETFs rank stocks within equities. Eight tickers do not equal eight independent exposures.

title: Economic mechanism and contribution
body:
Published hypotheses: delayed information, feedback and risk premia
Equity factor crashes: past losers rebound after panic states
ETF long/cash risks differ from short-loser equity momentum
Contribution: controlled comparisons with reproducible timing and accounting
notes: Daniel & Moskowitz 2016 introduction pp 221-223; Asness et al. 2014 Myth 10; Kolanovic & Wei 2015 pp 19-20. Published findings are motivation, not our measured returns. No new anomaly, sector neutrality or conditional-mean replication claimed.

title: Exact monthly holdings rule
body:
Universe: SPY EFA EEM IEF TLT GLD DBC VNQ
Rank 12-month total returns; choose top 3
Each 1/3 slot invests only if its return exceeds matched cash
Example signals 12%, 8%, 1%; cash 2% -> two 1/3 ETFs +1/3 cash
Vol 16% -> q 0.625 ->20.83%, 20.83%, 58.33% cash
notes: Signals use comparable penultimate monthly snapshots, not 252 days. Alphabetical tie break. No refill or renormalization. Worked numbers here are illustrative arithmetic, not historical signals. Actual decisions and endpoints are in etf_signals.csv; see notebook 2.

title: Risk cap and opportunity cost
body:
B3 estimates 126-day gross B2 excess volatility
q=min(1, 10%/max(volatility, 5%)); remainder cash
Average cash 22.82% versus B2 5.22%
Protection reduces upside and does not guarantee maximum loss
notes: Forecast is trailing strategy volatility, not a current-holdings covariance forecast. Monthly decisions persist; weights drift. B3 never leverages to reach 10%. Baltas & Kosowski 2013 section 3 motivates volatility normalization, but futures positions and estimator differ.

title: Data, timing and historical validation
body:
Real French, Cboe and Yahoo/yfinance snapshots
September cutoff; French RF/Mom available only through August
Signal penultimate close -> execute final close -> next-session return
All 8 ETF history begins 2006; B3 warmup -> September 2007 returns
Development to 2013 | validation 2014-19 | historical holdout 2020-26
notes: ETF first common execution 2007-08-31; first invested return 2007-09-04. Factor first execution 1990-01-31; first return 1990-02-01. RF cash endpoints bind August 31. Adj Close includes distributions; no double counting. Current vintages may revise history. Holdout is publicly known and inspected.

title: Lower drawdown comes with lower return
body:
Relative selection improves historical return over equal weighting
Absolute filter scarcely improves worst drawdown here
Volatility cap provides the strongest ETF drawdown reduction
B3 trails SPY and 60/40 in full-history CAGR
notes: ETF capital: 2007-08-31 execution inception to 2026-08-31; modeled net 10 bps/traded dollar. Comparing component risks and mean exposures prevents presenting lower cash-adjusted risk as costless alpha. B1 CAGR8.66%, B2 7.95%, B3 6.89%; values trace to performance.csv.

title: Robustness and uncertainty
body:
Historical holdout B3: CAGR 10.46% | Sharpe 0.805
B3-minus 60/40 Sharpe 95% CI: [-0.598, 0.279]
Skip-month diagnostic worsens drawdown; gold exclusion hurts
All 84 ledger rows retained; stronger 9-month result is not adopted
notes: 1000 paired moving-block draws, 6-month blocks, seed 9339. No future out-of-sample claim; cross-strategy selection inspected holdout. Sensitivity common start 2007-10-31 accommodates skip-month warmup. CI includes zero; resampling historical returns does not remove selection bias.

title: Costs, liquidity and mandate size
body:
B3 turnover 3.15x NAV/year; assumed 10 bps per dollar
1m/10m/50m AUM scenarios evolve with net NAV
10m B3 maximum DBC participation 19.17% of lagged ADV20
All-day vendor ADV does not certify closing-auction capacity
Validate 1m scenario first;10m single-close fills are not established
notes: Participation from raw Close*Volume through snapshot, abs delta weights, pretrade evolving NAV. Cost is an assumption, not measured spread.1%/5% ADV are illustrative constraints. Auction/impact/underlying liquidity and independent data checks needed. Taxes and investor fees excluded.

title: Evidence-supported advantages and risks
body:
Advantages: explicit holdings, fixed rules, no leverage, cash audit
B3 reduced losses in 2022; it missed upside in 2020
Risks: whipsaw, reversals, gold dependence and duration overlap
Higher full-sample Sharpe than 60/40 is not demonstrated
notes: 2020 B3 return 7.77% vs 60/40 15.99%;2022 B3 -5.03% vs 60/40 -16.67%. Daily exposure/cost files substantiate implementation transparency. This is a design advantage, not a claim of statistical alpha. Provider revisions and retrospective universe selection remain.

title: Proposed research mandate and investor Q&A
body:
Proposal: B3 research-stage risk-limited ETF design
Why more cash? It buys lower exposure and sacrifices return
Why not B1? Keep it as the higher-return comparator
Next milestone: independent data, auction costs, prospective paper signals
Feed failure: preserve holdings, verify data, escalate and log
notes: Raising assets remains the objective, with illustrative 10m contingent on evidence. No trades or assignment submission authorized. Suspend new decisions after material data/accounting defects, repeated operational failures or participation breaches; do not retrofit these rules into historical returns. Full investor Q&A is in report section 9.

title: Appendix | Factor experiment
body:
A0 gross synthetic CAGR 7.94% | drawdown -63.29%
A3 gross synthetic CAGR 11.99% | drawdown -18.89%
Bear 24 months + VIX>25 -> exposure 0 when both flags
RF + a*Mom: funding/borrow/internal turnover not measured
notes: A dates 1990-01-31 to 2026-08-31. French Mom six size/momentum portfolios, daily formed daily; monthly official series separate. Unit factor gross notional 2, cap 1.5 permits gross 3. A is not an executable stock strategy. Daniel-Moskowitz conditional mean/variance sizing is not replicated.

title: Appendix | Factor exposures and panic states
body:
A0=1 | A1=vol scale | A2=state scale | A3=combined
a_vol=min(1.5, 10%/max(sigma 126, 5%))
Market total return compounds Mkt-RF + RF
Published loser-rebound mechanism motivates the fixed heuristic
notes: Signals use past 24 comparable monthly snapshots and backward VIX. Exposure decisions held after execution; neither VIX nor market rebound from future periods enters signal. March-May 2009 static capital loses 45.64%; zero factor exposure avoids it in A2/A3. Internal Mom turnover, financing and borrow omitted.

title: Appendix | Accounting and statistical conventions
body:
Daily weights drift; rebalance only at execution close
T=sum risky |target-pretrade|; full A-to-B switch T=2
NAV_after=NAV_before*(1+gross)*(1-0.001*T)
Sharpe=sqrt(12)*mean(monthly excess)/sample_sd
CAGR ACT/365.25 | HAC3 | downside RMS Sortino
notes: Worked 50/50 drift example in report section 4 and tests. Targets are post-cost allocations using proportional NAV haircut. Initial execution charge combined into first holding month. Cash is compounded daily RF; empirical monthly VaR/ES loss-positive with tail count. Undefined Sharpe for deterministic excess cash.
